Length: |EF| = 28 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Among the given options sound waves travel fastest through:

• It is a mechanical wave that needs a medium to travel.
 
• The speed of sound is proportional to the density of the material.
 
• Since the density of a solid is maximum so the speed of sound is maximum in solid.
 
 

Speed of sound in solid (6000 m/s) > Speed of sound in liquid (1402 to 1482 m/s) > Speed of sound in gas/air (330 to 345 m/s).

EXPLANATION__:

 
• The distances between molecules in solids are very small, i.e., solids are denser - as compared to liquids and gases.
 
• Because they are so close, they can collide very quickly, i.e. it takes less time for a molecule of the solid to 'bump' into its neighbor.
 
• Solids are packed together tighter than liquids and gases, hence sound travels fastest in solids. 
 
• The **water** is liquid, so the speed of sound in water is less than that in steel.
 
• **Glycerin** is also a type of liquid so the sound speed is less than that in solid (steel).
 
• As the **steel is solid, so the sound waves travel fastest through it** and minimum in air. So option 4 is correct.

questions.question: Which type of radiation is widely used to sterilize consumer cosmetics such as hair products and contact lens solutions?

__
 
• The type of radiation that is widely used to sterilize consumer cosmetics such as hair products and contact lens solutions is **gamma radiation.**
 
• Gamma radiation is a form of ionizing radiation, which means that it can break **chemical bonds in DNA. **
 
• This damage to DNA can kill **microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses.**
 
• Gamma radiation is a very effective way to sterilize cosmetics because it can penetrate most materials, including **plastic, glass, and metal.**
 
• This means that the entire product can be sterilized, **even if it is sealed in its packaging.**
 
• Gamma radiation is also a **non-contact process,** which means that the product does not come into direct contact with any harmful chemicals or gases.
 
• The amount of gamma radiation that is needed to sterilize a product depends on the type of product and the level of contamination.
 
 
• In general, the **higher the level of contamination, the more radiation that is needed**. The gamma radiation dose is typically measured in **gray (Gy).** A gray is equal to one **joule of energy per kilogram of matter.**
 
 
 
• The FDA has set a maximum allowable dose of gamma radiation for cosmetics of **10 kGy.** This dose is well below the levels that are known to be harmful to humans.
 
• In addition to being effective and safe, gamma radiation is also a **relatively inexpensive way to sterilize cosmetics.** This makes it a cost-effective option for manufacturers of consumer products.***Hence option 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Beta rays** are negatively charged particles that are identical to electrons. They have a** higher penetrating power than alpha rays but a lower ionization power.**
 
• **Neutrons** are neutral particles that do not have a charge. They have the highest penetrating power of all types of radiation.

questions.question: In covering a distance of 162 km, Abhay takes 6 hours more than Sameer. If Abhay doubles his speed, then he would take 3 hours less than Sameer. Abhay's initial speed is:

**Given:**

Distance = 162 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let Abhay speed = a km/hr and Sameer speed = s km/hr

Abhay takes 6 hr more than Sameer: 162/a − 162/s = 6

If Abhay doubles speed, he takes 3 hr less than Sameer: 162/(2a) = 162/s − 3

⇒ 162/(2a) = 162/s − 3 ⇒ 81/a = 162/s − 3

⇒ From above 162/s = 81/a + 3

⇒ Substitute in first: 162/a &
;minus; (81/a + 3) = 6

⇒ 162/a − 81/a − 3 = 6

⇒ 81/a = 9

⇒ a = 81 ÷ 9 = 9 km/hr

**∴ Abhay's initial speed = 9 km/hr.**

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 20 days. If A alone can do it in 45 days, then B alone can do one-third of the same work in _______ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B finish work in 20 days

A alone finishes in 45 days

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(20, 45) = 180 units

Efficiency(A + B) = 180 ÷ 20 = 9 units/day

Efficiency(A) = 180 ÷ 45 = 4 units/day

Efficiency(B) = 9 − 4 = 5 units/day

B’s one-third work = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 units

Time taken = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ B alone can do one-third of work in 12 days.**

questions.question: In finding the HCF of two numbers by division method, the quotients are 1, 5, and 8, respectively, and the last divisor is 57. What is the LCM of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Quotients = 1, 5, 8

Last Divisor = 57

**Formula used:**

Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder

LCM(a, b) = (a × b) / HCF(a, b)

**Calculations:**

To find the two numbers, we'll work backward from the last division.

The last divisor is 57 and the remainder is 0 (since it's the HCF calculation).

Second to last divisor = 57 × 8 + 0 = 456

This divisor (456) is the remainder of the previous step. The second to last quotient is 5.

Third to last divisor = 456 × 5 + 57 = 2280 + 57 = 2337

This divisor (2337) is the remainder of the first step. The first quotient is 1.

First number = 2337 × 1 + 456 = 2337 + 456 = 2793

The two numbers are 2337 and 2793.

The HCF of these numbers is the last divisor, which is 57.

Now, we can calculate the LCM:

LCM = (2337 × 2793) / 57

⇒ LCM = 2337 × 49

⇒ LCM = 114513

**∴ The LCM of the two numbers is 114,513.**

questions.question: A bullet of mass 20 gm is fired from a rifle of mass 8 kg with a velocity of 100 m/s. The velocity of recoil of the rifle is:
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• **Momentum (P)**: The product of mass and velocity is called a momentum of the system.

Momentum (P) = Mass (m) × Velocity (V)

 
• Conservation of momentum: Whenever there is no net external force on the system then the total momentum of the system remains constant.

Initial momentum (P1) = Final momentum (P2)

CALCULATION__:

 
• As there is no external force on the pistol and bullet system. So the total momentum of the system will remain constant.

Initially the system was in rest so velocity (V) = 0

Initial momentum (P1) = mass (m) × Velocity (V) = m × 0 = 0

After firing,

Velocity of bullet (Vb) = 100 m/s

Mass of bullet (mb) = 20 g = 20/1000 = 0.02 kg

Momentum of bullet (Pb) = mb × Vb = 0.02 × 100 = 2 kg m/s

Let recoil velocity of pistol = V m/s

Mass of rifle (mr) = 8 kg

Momentum of rifle (Pr) = mr × V = 8 × V = 8V kg m/s

Total final momentum of the system (P2) = Momentum of rifle + momentum of bullet = (8V + 2) kg m/s

According to conservation of momentum;

Initial momentum (P1) = Final momentum (P2)

0 = 8V + 2

V = - 2/8 = - 1/4 = - 0.25 m/s

The negative sign denotes opposite direction. So the **recoil velocity of pistol is 0.25 m/s.**

Hence option 4 is correct.

• Deviation without Dispersion (Achromatic Prism): It is possible to combine two prisms of different materials in such a way that each cancels the dispersion due to the other. Thus, the net dispersion is zero but a deviation is produced. The required condition is

(μv – μr) A = (μ′v - μ′r) A′

Where for the first prism: μv = refractive index of the medium in violet light, μr = refractive index of the medium in red light A = angle of the prism; For the second prism: μ′v = refractive index of the medium in violet light, μ′r = refractive index of the medium in red light, A’ = angle of prism.)

μr = 1.513, μb = 1.523 for crown glass and μ'r = 1.645, μ'b = 1.665 for flint glass

A = 6°

 
• The required condition for **Achromatic prism** is:

(μb – μr) A = (μ′b - μ′r) A′

(1.523 - 1.513) × 6 = (1.665 - 1.645) A'

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward and it reaches the greatest height in 1 sec. Find the distance travelled by it during the first 1/4 sec of its descent from the greatest height.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Equation of motion: The mathematical equations used to find the final velocity, displacements, time, etc of a moving object without considering force acting on it are called equations of motion.
 
• These equations are only valid when the acceleration of the body is constant and they move on a straight line.

There are three equations of motion:

V = u + at

V2 = u2 + 2 a S

{{S}} = {{ut}} + (1)/(2){{a}}{{{t}}²}

Where, V = final velocity, u = initial velocity, s = distance traveled by the body under motion, a = acceleration of body under motion, and t = time taken by the body under motion.

CALCULATION__:

Given that:

Time taken to reach maximum height (t) = 1 sec

At maximum height, velocity = 0 = final velocity (v)

**a = - g (acceleration due to gravity**, it is negative becasue it is in downward direction and ball is thrown in upward direction)

Let u is initial velocity

Use v = u + a t 

0 = u - g × 1

So u = g

Now use V2 = u2 + 2 a S

0 = g² - 2g S

So S = g²/2g = g/2

Now the **ball is droped**:

Initial velocity (u) = 0

time (t) = 1/4 sec

a = g (it is positive becasue it is in downward direction and ball is also moving in downward direction)

Use {{S}} = {{ut}} + (1)/(2){{a}}{{{t}}²}

⇒ {{S}} = {{ut}} + (1)/(2){{a}}{{{t}}²} = 0 + (1)/(2)times g times (1/4)²

So the **distance traveled in first 1/4 second = S = g/32** 

Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.question: A particle of mass m is moving with a uniform speed v in a circle of radius r. What is the work done by the centripetal force after three complete turns?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Circular Motion: The movement of an object along a circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path is called circular motion.
 
• Uniform circular motion: The circular motion in which the speed of the particle remains constant is called uniform circular motion. In a uniform circular motion, force supplies the centripetal acceleration.
 
 
• The kinetic energy and the speed of the body remain constant.
 
 

If the Force F acts on a body and it gets displaced by a displacement of S, the work done in that case is given by:

Work done (W) = FS Cos θ

 
• Centripetal Force: It is a force required to move a body uniformly in a circle. This force acts along the radius and towards the center of the circle.

{bf{Centripetal}} {bf{Force}} ( {bf{F}} ) = frac{{m{v²}}}{r}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f46b912f41ec25deef8dbc2e5fe66a30340ac0dc320abb2c6b38a9c3275c5aaf.png] 

 
• The centripetal force required for circular motion along the surface of the road, towards the center of the turn. The Static friction between tire and road provides the necessary centripetal force.

CALCULATION__:

 
• The movement is uniform circular in motion. The angle between force and displacement is 90°. The force and displacement are perpendicular to each other

⇒ cos 90° = 0

Work done (W) = FS Cos 90° = 0 J
